newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Proventus challenges Danes for glassmaker.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Proventus challenges Danes for glassmaker.

text.p: Swedish investment group Proventus on Friday challenged a possible bid by Danish Royal Copenhagen for control of stylish Swedish glassmaker Orrefors Kosta Boda AB.

Proventus AB said before the Stockholm bourse opened on Friday that it had increased its stake in the fashionable Swedish firm to 21.1 percent and had bought an option for a further 9.1 percent, giving it a 30.2 percent holding.
Later on Friday, Proventus said it was bidding for a further 20 percent to give it a majority stake.
Proventus, in a challenge to the Danish porcelain, silver and glass producer Royal Copenhagen AS bid 145 crowns ($24.7) per share, a 26 percent premium over Thursday's close.

Orrefors' share was suspended early on Friday but the share rocketed when trading restarted, jumping 35 crowns to 150 crowns in light trade on market speculation Royal Copenhagen would launch a counter-bid.

"For a while Proventus has been working on a solution which would allow Proventus to take control of Orrefors Kosta Boda to actively support the company industrially and financially in its continued development," Proventus said in a statement.

Royal Copenhagen said on Wednesday it had bought 460,000 shares in Orrefors, giving it a total of 618,606 shares or 17.1 percent of the company, saying the purchase should be seen as underlining its interest in cooperating with Orrefors.
Proventus, which has a stake in the Puma sportswear company, said it was aware of the acquisition.

"The logic behind the purchase means it cannot be ruled out that Royal Copenhagen has ambitions to increase its stake in Orrefors Kosta Boda to create a Danish-controlled corporation," Proventus added.

Orrefors Kosta Boda and Royal Copenhagen announced in July they would work together to improve distribution and boost sales in key U.S. and European export markets and try to expand sales networks into South America and Eastern Europe.

Royal Copenhagen, which is 82 percent owned by Danish brewer Carlsberg A/S, is a world leader in artistic glassware, porcelain and silverware including jewellery from internationally renowned designer Georg Jensen.
Proventus, controlled by Swedish financier Robert Weil, said its offer gave Orrefors expansion opportunities.

"As part of a multinational group with a large number of similar brand names, Orrefors would probably risk receiving less attention and resources than if it became an independent industrial company with an active and financially strong owner."

Proventus managing director Mikael Kamras said the company was prepared to inject capital into the company if it was needed, but added it was too early to tell if Orrefors was in need of a capital boost.
"If the company needs more capital, Proventus is ready to come up with it," Kamras told Reuters.
Kamras said the company had tried to bid for the entire company but that this was not now possible. Weil owns 91.5 percent of Proventus and Kamras owns 8.5 percent.
As of July 27, the Swedish Wallenberg business empire owned 23.1 percent of the share capital and votes of Orrefors. Proventus was the second largest owner.
Proventus also owns 25 percent of Puma, Swedish sports shoe and tennis ball maker Tretorn, Finnish furniture company Artek, and printing and textile activities. ($1=5.865 Danish Crown)
